'''Nils Aall Barricelli''' (24 January 1912 – 27 January 1993) was a [[Norwegians|Norwegian]]-[[Italians|Italian]] [[mathematician]].

== Biography ==
Nils Aall Barricelli was born on 24 January 1912, in Rome. When he was a student at the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]], he "studied mathematics and physics under [[Enrico Fermi]]". In 1936 he moved to Norway with his divorced mother and sister.<ref name="nautilus"/> In 1946, he wrote a PhD thesis "on the statistical analysis of climate variation". He did not get a degree - his thesis had 500 pages, and the committee suggested that he shorten it. He declined and never completed his PhD.<ref name="cabinetmagazine"/><ref name="nautilus">{{cite web |last1=Hackett |first1=Robert |title=Meet the Father of Digital Life |url=https://nautil.us/meet-the-father-of-digital-life-234937/ |website=Nautilus |access-date=4 January 2024 |date=30 May 2014}}</ref> In 1951, he submitted an application for [[Fulbright Scholarship]].<ref name="nautilus"/><ref name="cabinetmagazine"/> He wrote a short biography in the application:<ref name="cabinetmagazine">{{cite web |last1=Galloway |first1=Alexander R. |title=Creative Evolution {{!}} Alexander R. Galloway |url=https://www.cabinetmagazine.org/issues/42/galloway.php |website=cabinetmagazine.org |access-date=4 January 2024 |language=en}}</ref>
<blockquote>
In 1932 I passed the Italian Artium examination (classical line), and in 1936 the Italian graduation in Mathematical and physical sciences. In 1936 I settled in Norway where I have been working with scientific researches in theoretical statistics and stationary time series ... [and the] mathematical theory of evolution. ... Since 1947 I have been Assistant Professor at the [[University of Oslo]].
</blockquote>

[[Ragnar Frisch]], who later won [[Nobel Prize in Economics]], wrote a letter recommending him to [[John von Neumann]].<ref name="nautilus"/>

Barricelli's early computer-assisted experiments<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Barricelli|first=Nils Aall|date=1954|title=Esempi numerici di processi di evoluzione|journal=Methodos|volume=6|pages=45–68}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | volume=16| number=1–2 | year=1962 | pages=69–98 | doi=10.1007/BF01556771 | journal= Acta Biotheoretica | title= Numerical testing of evolution theories : Part I Theoretical introduction and basic tests | last1=Barricelli | first1=Nils Aall | s2cid=124273411 }}</ref> in [[symbiogenesis]] and [[evolution]] are considered pioneering in [[artificial life]] research. Barricelli, who was independently wealthy, held an unpaid residency at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]] in 1953, 1954, and 1956. In Princeton, he worked with [[John von Neumann]], by whom he was never academically recognised, nonetheless he worked at von Neumann's [[IAS machine]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Biology at the Institute for Advanced Study - Ideas {{!}} Institute for Advanced Study |url=https://www.ias.edu/ideas/2008/dyson-biology |website=www.ias.edu |access-date=4 January 2024 |language=en |date=30 June 2015}}</ref><ref name="nautilus"/><ref>Dyson, George. 1997. Darwin Among the Machines. Reading, MA: Helix Books, p. 111</ref><ref>Dyson, George. 2012. Turing's Cathedral: The Origins of the Digital Universe. Pantheon Books, Chapter 6, p. 225</ref>

[[George Dyson (science historian)|George Dyson]] described Barricelli's first experiments at Princeton:<ref>{{cite web |title=An Artificially Created Universe - Ideas {{!}} Institute for Advanced Study |url=https://www.ias.edu/ideas/2012/george-dyson-ecp |website=www.ias.edu |access-date=4 January 2024 |language=en |date=3 May 2012}}</ref>
<blockquote>
At 10:38 p.m. on March 3, 1953, in a one-story brick building at the end of Olden Lane in Princeton, New Jersey, Italian-Norwegian mathematical biologist Nils Aall Barricelli inoculated a 5-kilobyte digital universe with random numbers generated by drawing playing cards from a shuffled deck. "A series of numerical experiments are being made with the aim of verifying the possibility of an evolution similar to that of living organisms taking place in an artificially created universe," he announced.
</blockquote>

He later worked at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], at [[Vanderbilt University]] (until 1964), in the Department of Genetics of the [[University of Washington]], Seattle (until 1968) and then at the Mathematics Institute of the [[University of Oslo]]. Barricelli published in a variety of fields including [[virus]] genetics,<ref name="nautilus"/> [[DNA]], [[theoretical biology]], [[space flight]], [[theoretical physics]] and [[Mathematical notation|mathematical language]].<ref>{{cite web |title=THE REALITY CLUB Darwin Among the Machines Or, The Origins of Artificial Life A Presentation by George Dyson |url=http://www.edge.org/discourse/dysong_darwin.html |website=edge.org |access-date=4 January 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120527064633/http://www.edge.org/discourse/dysong_darwin.html |archive-date=27 May 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
Barricelli is mostly forgotten,<ref name="nautilus"/><ref name=fogel/> though he is sometimes called the "Father of Digital Life".<ref name="nautilus"/> He is recognised as a first person who programmed the first [[genetic algorithm]],<ref>{{cite book |last1=Simon |first1=Dan |title=Evolutionary Optimization Algorithms |date=13 June 2013 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-1-118-65950-2 |page=42 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gwUwIEPqk30C&pg=PA42 |access-date=4 January 2024 |language=en}}</ref> and published "perhaps the earliest published record of an evolutionary simulation" in 1954.<ref name=fogel>{{cite journal |last1=Fogel |first1=D.B. |title=Historic perspective - Nils Barricelli-artificial life, coevolution, self-adaptation |journal=IEEE Computational Intelligence Magazine |date=February 2006 |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=41–45 |doi=10.1109/MCI.2006.1597062 }}</ref>

He is featured in [[George Dyson (science historian)|George Dyson]]'s books ''Turing's Cathedral'' and ''Darwin Among the Machines'',<ref name="nautilus"/> and in [[Benjamin Labatut]]'s novel ''[[The MANIAC]]''.<ref name="globe">{{cite web |last1=Donaldson |first1=Emily |title=With The MANIAC, author Benjamin Labatut dives into the path of madness |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/arts/books/article-with-the-maniac-author-benjamin-labatut-dives-into-the-path-of-madness/ |publisher=The Globe and Mail |access-date=3 January 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20231008112848/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/arts/books/article-with-the-maniac-author-benjamin-labatut-dives-into-the-path-of-madness/ |archive-date=8 October 2023 |language=en-CA |date=6 October 2023}}</ref>
